question: On scraping a psoriatic plaque, silvery scale flakes off (candle-grease sign) and further gentle scraping of the exposed membrane produces discrete pinpoint bleeding. What is the structural basis of this Auspitz sign?

answers.text: The suprapapillary epidermis is thinned to two to three cell layers over elongated dermal papillae carrying dilated, tortuous capillary loops

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In psoriasis the epidermis overlying the dermal papillae is markedly reduced, and those papillae carry dilated capillaries — scraping through this thin roof exposes the capillaries and produces the characteristic discrete pinpoint bleeding points.

answers.text: Fragile intraepidermal blisters rupture on minimal friction, releasing serosanguinous fluid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Blister rupture with minimal shearing force describes the Nikolsky sign seen in pemphigus and toxic epidermal necrolysis, not the Auspitz sign of psoriasis.

answers.text: Thrombosed superficial veins in the reticular dermis are exposed by deep scraping

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The bleeding in the Auspitz sign originates from dilated capillaries in the elongated dermal papillae just below the epidermis, not from deeper reticular dermal veins.

answers.text: Neutrophilic micro-abscesses in the stratum corneum burst on the surface

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in the parakeratotic scale) are a histological feature of psoriasis, they are not the source of pinpoint bleeding — the exposed papillary capillaries are.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the structural basis: in psoriasis the suprapapillary epidermis is thinned to two to three cell layers over elongated dermal papillae carrying dilated capillary loops — scraping through this thin roof exposes the capillaries, producing pinpoint bleeding.

Excellent. The Auspitz sign is a direct consequence of psoriatic architecture — elongated dermal papillae with dilated capillaries sitting beneath a markedly thinned suprapapillary epidermis of just two to three cell layers.
